newsitem.title: USA: Flood victims urge Congress to pass relief bill.
newsitem.headline: Flood victims urge Congress to pass relief bill.

text.p: Flood victims from the Midwest urged Congress Tuesday to pass a disaster relief bill free of any unrelated measures to get $5.4 billion in aid out to 35 states.

President Clinton Monday vetoed an $8.6 billion spending bill, including $5.4 billion in disaster aid, saying he could not accept two provisions that Republicans added to it aiming to prevent government shutdowns and block a change in census-taking.
Congress put off voting on the bill before a one-week break last month because of the expected veto.

"This is an example of making us victims twice. Once by the flood, and then once again by politics," said Allan Kantrud of Grand Forks, N.D., who, like thousands of others, had to abandon his home during floods in April.
"All of the things that they're adding to this bill is making it impossible for the president to sign," said Doris Wilson, a Sierra Club member from Louisville, Ky., whose home was also flooded.
The Sierra Club said as of June, 35 people were killed in flooding this year. More than 500 died in floods over the last five years.
Flood damage so far this year had reached about $2.75 billion, and more than $34 billion since 1993, according to Brett Hulsey, the group's Midwest representative.
The Sierra Club blamed the massive flooding on regulations that allow farmers and land developers to destroy wetlands, which soak up rain and snow.

The group urged the Clinton administration to help limit flood damage by not issuing any new land development permits that might harm wetlands, until permit restrictions are reviewed, and cutting federal flood insurance subsidies for new homes on wetlands or floodplains.
It also called for the government to increase funding for a wetlands reserve programme and the Conservation Reserve Programme, which pays farmers not to cultivate fragile land.
